entries.findingHeading: 1. **A schema-valid topic ID can create an invalid SVG attribute name.** `ScopeAperture/ScopeTopic.tsx:36` places `topic.id` inside the attribute name `data-topic-position-${topic.id}`, while `ScopeAperture/ScopeAperture.schema.ts:10` intentionally accepts any nonempty string up to 20 characters. A focused read-only SSR probe using `id: "topic with space"` passed validation, then emitted `Invalid attribute name: data-topic-position-topic with space`; React dropped that attribute. The drawing and `data-topic` identity remained intact, so this is not a visual failure. Use fixed attributes such as `data-topic`, `data-x` and `data-y` and have tests select by the escaped attribute value. Preserve the catalog's ID bounds rather than narrowing the schema. The coordinator has recorded this for final triage.

entries.findingHeading: #### M1. Accepted custody seal touches the first dense detail line
entries.exactFindingText:
#### M1. Accepted custody seal touches the first dense detail line

**Locations:** `CustodyTransfer/CustodyAcceptance.tsx:12`, `CustodyTransfer/CustodyObject.tsx:6`, `:34`.

The acknowledgment seal is centered at (680,230), radius 22, with a 2px stroke, so its painted bottom reaches y=253. The first detail begins at x=534 with a 14px font and baseline y=260, placing the top of its glyphs around y=250. Maximum-width detail text spans the seal's x position. The supplied `CustodyTransfer-dense-150.png` shows the lower seal edge touching/overpainting the first row of Ws. The semantic handoff remains clear, so this is local typography polish rather than a reason by itself to reject the task.

**Fix:** reserve a clear vertical gap between the seal and the adjoining details, and assert non-occlusion against their actual text rows. A focused accepted 28-character recipient probe also produces three holder-name lines with baselines 165, 188.4 and 211.8, so preserve room above the seal as well when choosing its revised position.

entries.findingHeading: **O1. Nonblocking pre-existing facade overlap near a later chosen entrance.**
entries.exactFindingText:
**O1. Nonblocking pre-existing facade overlap near a later chosen entrance.**

| Mobility | Current emitted head center | Distance to facade interior | Exterior overlap, including both strokes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wheelchair | (340, 340.3969513611947) | 5.3333333333310975px | 4.6666666666689025px |
| Walking | (340, 349.0000000000027) | 5.3333333333310975px | 4.6666666666689025px |

The focused probe used `inputSchema.parse({ ...denseInput, chosenServiceId: "1", accessChange: "clear-entrance", participantMobility })` for each mobility mode. Bisection of the actual emitted head x coordinate gave frame **92.9063036239042**, where the current head center is x339.9999999999978. The preceding, unchosen service has ID `"0"`. Its actual facade tag is:

```xml
<rect x="198.66666666666669" y="194"
      width="136" height="176" rx="8"
      fill="#101e28" stroke="#2a404e">
```

Head exterior radius: 9.5px (r8, stroke 3). Facade stroke: SVG default 1px. Both samples lie beside its straight right edge, outside the rounded corner.

**Base comparison from the immutable diff:** current x340 corresponds to approach progress `(340 - 60) / (380 - 60) = 0.875`. The base formula at `AccessParticipant.tsx:17` was `mix(approach, 90, doorX - 100)`, so the same frame placed the head at x343.75. The base floor was y356 for `clear-entrance`; the former body formula at lines19-21 placed the wheelchair head at y297 and walking head at y301. Both centers were also beside the facade's unchanged straight edge. The base distance was `343.75 - 334.6666666666667 = 9.0833333333333px`, less than the combined 10px exterior radius. Thus that base frame already overlapped the same facade by about **0.9166666666667px**. This is a retained visual collision with an existing entrance facade, not a newly introduced collision class or the specific filled obstruction fixed by N2. It does not reopen this correction loop. The controller should retain it for whole-branch visual triage.

entries.exactFindingText:
#### M1. Opening test names promise assertions that their bodies do not perform.

Later tests cover much of that behavior, so this is misleading naming rather than a claim that all coverage is missing. Name each opening test after its actual assertions, or move the full assertions into that test.

pass. These participant fields are excluded from the generic stress mutation,
so those helpers do not fill this gap for the locally supplied strings.

geometry, or narrow the test names to their actual accessibility-text claim.

Cost if wrong: source integration touches the listed legacy renderer files and the narrow shared copy/extraction boundary, requiring focused regression and revised source-closure hashes even though English behavior is unchanged.

supportingReportSection.heading: ## Confirmed gaps
supportingReportSection.exactText:
## Confirmed gaps

**SR-01: RevisionRestore.** Schema lines 28-47; rule lines 53-60. Saved-history compares selected and final positional content, but paths omit `revisions.*.content`. Its description already states content inequality. Minimal correction: add that content path to `saved-history.paths`.

**SR-02: ContactWindowOverlap.** Schema lines 49-74; rule lines 79-86. The rule omits increasing investigation-window ordering and investigation/record containment within `axis.end`. Stating 0..12 does not express an authored axis ending earlier. Minimal correction: export `investigationWindow.start < investigationWindow.end <= axis.end` and both-null records or `start < end <= axis.end`, with corresponding paths.

Source paths are under `apps/ava-video-producer/src/stock/presets/<Component>/<Component>.schema.ts`. Both corrections are metadata-only candidates. Preserve inclusive axis-end equality, both-null records and all runtime acceptance.

supportingReportSection.heading: ## Findings
supportingReportSection.exactText:
## Findings

**SR-03: NodeTraversal omits validity of unused edges.** `presets/legacy/legacyFields.ts`:34-42 validates every edge against authored node count and rejects self-edges. `NodeTraversal.contract.ts`:20-27 exports route indices and directed adjacency only. Add the existing NetworkGraph-style edge rule or extend that rule: every edge has distinct existing node endpoints. Paths: `nodes`, `edges`. Keep duplicate edges and all current runtime/default behavior.

**SR-04: Legacy text-fit rules omit quantitative details.** All 20 legacy contracts receive `fixed-text-slots` from `presets/legacy/createLegacyContract/createLegacyContract.ts`:27-35. It promises labels fit their declared sizes/slots, with wildcard path `*`. This provides conceptual coverage. It does not serialize the actual numerical budgets in the table below. This is one grouped precision finding, not 20 absent fit rules.

The missing cross-field detail includes CodeFocus concatenated token lines: UTF-16 length <=54 and conservative mono width <=718 at size 21. MetricCounter checks the concatenation of `value.toLocaleString("en-US")` and `unit`, width <=624 at size 103. WordReveal has position-specific masks: <=232 at91, <=236 at91 and <=414 at137. Export exact predicates and affected fields. Preserve accepted inputs and estimator behavior; do not add a width policy.

**All 10 additions have faithful machine-checkable rule text and affected paths.** The JSON contains all 30 comparisons, complete schema/contract source, 34 root callbacks, 53 text budgets and SHA-256 hashes for 67 inspected source files.

## Fixed-tuple structural export gap confirmed before integration

Controller read-only preflight found installed Zod draft-2020-12 `z.toJSONSchema(z.tuple(...))` emits `prefixItems` without array-length restrictions (`minItems`, `maxItems` or `items:false`). Source confirmed in installed zod/src/v4/core/json-schema-processors.ts tupleProcessor. A fixed two-item Zod runtime tuple rejects short/long values, while this JSON Schema shape admits them. Reviewed80-contract scan currently finds NestedDrilldownWindow records.*.groups and dimensions, and GisLayerIntersectionTally layers.*.polygon.*; later geographic packets may add more. See tuple-schema-preflight.json.

Before source freeze, correct structural export fidelity for every fixed tuple, covering both contract.jsonSchema and nested collection itemSchema consumed by the editor/export. Reuse z.toJSONSchema with a narrowly reviewed tuple-aware conversion or explicit representable cardinality as appropriate; do not change runtime acceptance or silently switch to a permissive target. Establish genuine RED/GREEN for missing/extra coordinates and fixed dimension tuples, preserving heterogeneous positional item schemas and any legitimate rest/optional tuple semantics. Ask controller for concrete shared-helper/source scope before broad changes. This is a confirmed contract-export gap, not a reason to narrow accepted inputs.

Additional read-only preflights in SDD workspace: control-path-preflight.json covers80contracts/1357controls/906defaultTextPaths (no unresolved paths; tuple-export gap separately required above). message-id-preflight.json checks4576descriptors/4550uniqueIDs with0conflicting-message collisions, excludinggenerated defaults/legacy20. select-reference-preflight.json checks405validfixtures/1838selects/728dynamic references/29emptyselections with0missingselectedoptions using actualselectOptions.
